name: Sylvester
editorial_article: Sylvester James, Jr. (1947–1988), known simply as Sylvester, was a trailblazing disco and queer icon whose influence on dance music remains profound. Born in the Watts neighborhood of Los Angeles, he was raised within the Pentecostal church, an environment that nurtured his early gospel singing. After moving to San Francisco in the late 1960s, Sylvester became a central figure in the avant-garde drag ensemble The Cockettes before transitioning into a solo career that bridged R&B, soul, and high-energy electronic dance music. He was celebrated for his flamboyant, androgynous persona and his remarkable high tenor voice, often cited as one of the first male "divas" of the disco era. His partnership with producer Patrick Cowley in the early 1980s was particularly transformative, helping to define the nascent Hi-NRG sound with tracks like "Do Ya Wanna Funk." Sylvester's legacy is marked by his open identity as a gay man during a time when such visibility was rare in pop music, and his 1978 hits "Dance (Disco Heat)" and "You Make Me Feel (Mighty Real)" remain cornerstones of club culture. He passed away from AIDS-related complications in 1988, but his artistry continues to be recognized for its expressive power and its central role in the evolution of modern dance floors. Throughout the late 70s and 80s, Sylvester challenged social norms by existing as an openly gay Black man who embraced androgyny and glamour in a mainstream, often hostile, music industry. His transition from rock-focused bands like the Hot Band to the electronic, club-oriented sound perfected by Cowley on the Megatone label shows his adaptability and commitment to the evolving queer club scene. Even after his death, his influence persists, with 'You Make Me Feel (Mighty Real)' serving as a perennial anthem. Today, he is remembered not just as a vocalist, but as a cultural figurehead who paved the way for future generations of queer artists, cementing his legacy through a discography that remains vibrant and essential to dance music history.
